title: Orvan growers point to a full wheat store after a dry spring

facts.subject: Orvan wheat harvest
facts.statement: Orvan farm groups expect a solid wheat harvest this season after a dry spring and a cool start to the growing year.

source_ref.text_snippet: Orvan farm groups expect a solid wheat harvest this season after a dry spring and a cool start to the growing year.

facts.subject: Wheat store
facts.statement: The crop is thin in places, but the store should be full.

source_ref.text_snippet: The crop is thin in places, but the store should be full.

facts.subject: Maize planting
facts.statement: Growers say maize planting is on schedule and that fuel and machinery costs remain the main concern.

source_ref.text_snippet: Growers say maize planting is on schedule and that fuel and machinery costs remain the main concern.

facts.subject: Harvest estimate
facts.statement: The ministry has not published a harvest estimate.

source_ref.text_snippet: The ministry has not published a harvest estimate.

facts.subject: Wheat and maize harvest
facts.statement: The union says the rain came at the right time for the wheat, though the west is still drier than the east.

source_ref.text_snippet: The union says the rain came at the right time for the wheat, though the west is still drier than the east.

facts.subject: Maize harvest schedule
facts.statement: It expects the maize harvest to begin on schedule.

source_ref.text_snippet: It expects the maize harvest to begin on schedule.

facts.subject: Domestic flour demand
facts.statement: Local buyers say domestic flour demand is steady.

source_ref.text_snippet: Local buyers say domestic flour demand is steady.
